characterization_methods.key_findings: The 15Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 6 h has a Vickers hardness of 862.8 ± 11.3 HV; hardness at 625 and 650 °C stabilized between 800 and 900 HV with prolonged aging time.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness (HV) of the solution-treated and aged samples

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification
characterization_methods.key_findings: The solution-treated alloys are single-phase α (BCC); during aging the α matrix transforms to β-Mn and new BCC and FCC phases precipitate within the β-Mn. For the 15Al alloy the α → β-Mn transformation is complete within 1 h at 600 °C and above (so also at 650 °C).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol); phase maps interpreted with legend BCC(red), α-Mn(blue), β-Mn(green), FCC(magenta)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the constituent phases and the α → β-Mn transformation in the aged alloys

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 15Al alloy the α → β-Mn transformation accelerates with aging temperature; at 600 °C and above the α matrix is almost completely transformed into β-Mn even after short aging times.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples; SE images used to identify α-Mn and β-Mn precipitates
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal the precipitation/transformation of second phases in the aged 15Al alloy

interfaces.interface_notes: For the ultra-hard Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys, new BCC phase and FCC Cu-rich phase form at the interfaces between the β-Mn. As β-Mn is an Mn-rich phase, its nucleation/growth enriches Mn while expelling Fe, Al and Cu into the surrounding matrix; the BCC phase is attributed to Al enrichment (a BCC stabilizer) around β-Mn interfaces, while the Cu-rich phase forms due to the limited solubility of Cu in Fe-based alloys. TEM of a fully transformed 15Al condition shows the fine particles at the β-Mn interfaces are FCC and rich in Cu, depleted in Fe and Mn and slightly poor in Al.
interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots with the nominal composition Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting raw materials with high purity (>99.9 %) in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
The solution-treated 15Al alloy was aged at 650 °C for 6 h, followed by water quenching; 650 °C aging is one of the six aging temperatures (525–650 °C) studied at 1, 3, 6 and 10 h.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness measured on an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the values averaged

phases_present.morphology: dominant/matrix phase; near-equiaxed β-Mn after complete α→β-Mn transformation
fine particles ('New BCC phase') at the interfaces between β-Mn
fine particles distributed at the interfaces between the β-Mn; FCC twins frequently observed within the particles

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 650 °C for 6 h the 15Al alloy's α matrix has almost completely transformed into β-Mn, and abundant fine precipitates (identified as BCC and FCC phases) are present within the β-Mn. Hardness at this condition is stabilized in the 800–900 HV range (625 °C and 650 °C plateau).

unmapped_findings: The paper reports a volume fraction of 3.9 % for the FCC Cu-rich and BCC phases in the 15Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 3 h (hardness 852.3 HV, b0069); this value corresponds to the 3 h condition and no such value is reported for the 650 °C / 6 h condition, so it is not assigned to this sample.

The 15Al alloy's flagship performance figures — the ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g, the fracture toughness KIC of 8.6 MPa·m^1/2 and the nanoindentation hardnesses (11.7 ± 0.4 GPa average, 12.1 ± 0.3 GPa intrinsic β-Mn) — belong to its peak-hardness condition (600 °C / 6 h, 965.6 HV) and are therefore not assigned to this 650 °C / 6 h sample (b0021, b0023, b0060, b0061, b0077).
